findings.text: Deferred fault handling uses a work item that can sit on two intrusive lists at once, points at the faulting virtual CPU, records the fault position in guest and host virtual forms, carries an architecture specific extension, and holds two flags that control broadcast wakeup scope and whether a not-present event was already delivered.

A guest frame interval for memory notifications names its slot and half open bounds, transports notifier attributes through a one member union, selects shared or private pages through a two value filter, and advertises whether the current context may block and whether it runs without strong locking.

Host mapping for one guest frame keeps optional pinned and unpinned page references with a host virtual address, host and guest frame numbers, plus a writability flag, where pin validity is limited to host managed memory as explained in the note about unmanaged guest memory.
Fragmented memory mapped input output is described per chunk by guest physical address with host data pointer, staged value, and byte length, allowing one logical access to span several entries.

Each virtual CPU anchors to its virtual machine and tracks host CPU, userspace identifier, array index, execution mode, request bits, debug controls, a private mutex, shared run area, sleep support, process identity under a dedicated read write lock, signal masking state, and halt polling configuration.

The virtual CPU tail adds optional fragmented input output state, queued and completed asynchronous fault lists under a spinlock with a queued count, optional spin loop hints for directed yield eligibility, scheduling and readiness flags, architecture and statistics areas, an identifier string, a dirty ring, and a cached memslot plus generation that assumes no practical wraparound.

A memory slot carries dual indexed identity plus host virtual interval and guest frame tree nodes, with base frame, page count, dirty bitmap pointer, architecture extension, userspace address, flags, numeric slot and address space identifiers, and an optional guest memfd file reference with page offset.

Interrupt routing entries map a global number and type through a level setting callback, then select one payload among irqchip pin pairing, message signaled address data flags and device identity, s390 adapter addresses offsets and identifier, hypervisor synthetic interrupt target, or Xen event channel port priority and virtual CPU linkage, all linkable in a hash list.

The routing table holds a two dimensional irqchip pin matrix with an entry count and a flexible array of hash heads indexed by global interrupt number, where each head chains the chips connected to that number.

One address space generation groups a monotonic generation number, an atomic last used slot hint, host virtual and guest frame search trees, a small fixed width hash from slot identifier to slot, and an index selecting which dual tree node set is active.

The virtual machine object centralizes memory management locking, userspace address space binding, active and inactive slot sets per address space with read copy update pointers, a virtual CPU array, dirty logging counters, invalidation sequencing state, guest physical cache management, CPU counts, global and slot locks, and input output buses.

Remaining virtual machine state covers interrupt descriptors with resampling support, event descriptors, statistics and architecture areas, reference counting, optional coalesced rings and zones, interrupt routing and acknowledgement lists, memory and power notifiers, device and dirty log bookkeeping, debug filesystem handles, two sleepable read copy update domains, userspace identity, halt polling tunables, dirty ring sizing, bug and dead markers, plus optional memory attribute storage.
Ordered slot traversal uses an iterator holding the slot set with current tree node and resolved slot pointer, advancing in guest frame order and resolving each node through the active node index.

Interrupt acknowledgement uses a hash node plus global number and callback, while statistics queries distinguish machine scope from virtual CPU scope and bind a machine pointer to a descriptor for debug filesystem exposure.
Short lived guest mapping bundles the target virtual CPU with an embedded host map and a status code, so scoped helpers can automatically release the mapping when the status shows success.

Virtual CPU mode cycles among outside guest, inside guest, and exiting guest, with a separate reading shadow page tables value for table inspection; entry and exit helpers bracket guest execution with timing and context transitions while preserving interrupt state.

Slot sets evolve as create, delete, move, or flags only changes against dual active and inactive copies selected by node index and generation, and range scans locate the upper bound above the start then step back one entry, skip a non overlapping predecessor, and stop once a slot starts at or beyond the requested end.

Asynchronous faults progress from queued to done lists with a queued count, fragmented input output progresses through current and total fragment counters with completion flags for read versus write, and dirty tracking toggles between single and dual bitmap halves plus an optional ring with bitmap mode.

Slot mutation serializes on a slots mutex with a nested architecture slot mutex that may instead be taken inside a sleepable read copy update read section to avoid deadlock with slot swap synchronization, while translation updates serialize on a memory management lock that is a read write lock where available and a spinlock otherwise, and slot readers use the sleepable domain.

Fine grained exclusion assigns a mutex per virtual CPU and per virtual machine, a spinlock plus resampling mutex for interrupt descriptors, an interrupt lock for routing updates, a spinlock for the coalesced ring, a spinlock for guest physical caches, a spinlock for invalidation counts with a wait primitive for slot updates, a read write lock for process identity, and a spinlock for asynchronous fault queues.
Guest boundary helpers provide interrupt disabled entry and exit plus an interrupt saving exit wrapper, intended to be called around the actual transition to and from guest execution.

Slot query helpers report emptiness from the guest frame tree, derive a slot identifier from a frame, convert host virtual addresses to guest frames via slot base arithmetic, and test whether a guest physical address currently maps through the host virtual translation.

Guest memory accessors expose pinned page lookup by frame, fault-in with optional write and writability outputs plus optional reference counted page, checked host virtual get and put that fault on invalid mappings and dirty on successful writes, and a read only virtual CPU mapping built on the general mapping primitive.

Default architecture shims allocate and free the machine object with accounted zeroed storage, report unsupported errors for remote translation flush with and without range, treat noncoherent direct memory access registration as absent, report the interrupt controller as initialized, turn performance and interrupt descriptor setup into no operations in one configuration, and make acknowledgement list updates and debug filesystem creation empty.

Diagnostic and statistics helpers prefix kernel and virtual CPU messages with process or virtual CPU identity and build descriptors from type unit base exponent size and bucket fields, deriving offsets into generic or architecture portions of machine and virtual CPU statistics with scope wrappers for cumulative instant peak histogram counter boolean and nanosecond time forms.

The second dirty bitmap immediately follows the first by its byte size, guest memfd support always advertises mapping with conditional shared initialization depending on architecture support and machine presence, manual dirty logging capability equals the manual protect enable value, and the scoped mapping class selects the read only or writable mapping variant by name suffix.

Each slot exists simultaneously in identifier, host virtual, and guest frame indexes with two node copies selected by the set index, identifier lookup uses a seven bit hash sized for several hundred slots, cached slot validity rides on generation comparison, and identifier plus address space fields disambiguate overlapping guest ranges.

Host virtual to guest frame conversion shifts the address delta by page size and adds the slot base, guest get splits physical addresses into frame plus page offset before checked host access, iteration validity requires a live node and a slot start strictly below the range end, and empty sets are detected by an empty guest frame tree.

Callers must not use the raw sleepable read copy update index directly, must not assume pin validity for unmanaged host frame numbers, must treat invalid host virtual translations as faults, must expect allocation and mapping failures, and must respect that the flexible routing map length is bound to its entry count while slot generation relies on practically non overflowing counters.
Maximum guest memory size in pages is one less than two raised to the thirty first power.
Internal slot reservation is zero, total slots equal SHRT_MAX, and user visible slots equal total minus internal.

Manual dirty logging capability equals KVM_DIRTY_LOG_MANUAL_PROTECT_ENABLE, the frame range filter uses bit zero for shared and bit one for private, the notifier attribute union carries an unsigned long, and virtual CPU mode members occupy four successive ordinals starting at zero for outside, inside, exiting, and shadow table reading.
